## 2026-06-06 04:55 CEST - audit/yul-object-source-language-completeness

Object-source grammar inventory: supported and theorem-covered constructs are `Expr.call`, `Expr.var`, `Expr.lit`, `Expr.datasize`, `Expr.dataoffset`, `Expr.datacopy`, statement blocks, declarations, assignments, expression statements, switches, fors, ifs, `continue`, `break`, `leave`, function definitions, dispatcher/functions, named data sections, and nested objects. The independent interpreter is `ObjectModel.Source`, not a lower-then-run adapter: object layout lives in `Runtime`, `datasize`/`dataoffset` read that layout, `datacopy` evaluates its object-source operands and executes source-level `CODECOPY` over `ExecutionEnv.codeBytes`, and internal calls dispatch through the source contract. Rejections are source-validity/lower-layer-boundary rejections rather than object-proof shortcuts: duplicate function names fail `functionMap?`, unresolved layout names fail builtin evaluation/lowering, unstable payload layout or failed bytecode-image computation prevents a checked object runtime, and `Program.Accepted`/`SourceAccepted` defer lower core/object compiler acceptedness to the already-existing lower layer. Public theorem boundary is source-facing for successful live `.Ok shared store` runs and has no caller-supplied object layout/replay certificate; remaining assumptions in `RecursiveBridgeObjectTopAssumptions` are the normal lower core-Yul compiler/runtime premises for the computed core program.

## 2026-06-02 - theorem-boundary/live-result-sensitive-handler-cleanup

Audited the remaining handler-live subset premises after the selected-switch scoping checkpoint. The current trim adapter preserves a full `LiveCtxCleanupRel`, so it asks for both break and continue handler retention before entering a nested body. That cannot be derived from arbitrary successful source runs: regular/leave/halt paths need no break/continue cleanup, while break and continue paths need only their matching handler state relation. The next sound tightening is therefore a result-sensitive open-block bridge/callback surface, not a theorem that both handler live sets are present for every accepted run.
